newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria says will meet Maastricht criteria in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Austria says will meet Maastricht criteria in 1997.

text.p: Austria said on Tuesday its federal budget deficit was projected to fall to 2.7 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997, putting the country on course for membership in Europe's planned single currency.
Finance Minister Viktor Klima told a news conference the country's deficit would fall to 68 billion schillings in 1997, from 89.4 billion schillings or 3.7 percent of GDP last year.
"Our aim for 1997 is to cut the budget deficit to 68 billion schillings," he said. "It seems possible."
The minister added he was convinced Austria would meet the Maastricht criteria for membership in Europe's planned economic and monetary union (EMU) in 1997.
"1997 is going to be a very important year in order to meet the Maastricht criteria, and we will actually make it," he said. "It would be a catastrophe if Austria were not in EMU."
Candidates for EMU membership are scheduled to be selected in spring 1998 on the basis of 1997 economic performance.
